builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
summary: The method replaces prompting an unadapted small edge model for domain-specific code generation with QLoRA/LoRA supervised fine-tuning on a small checked dataset, deployed as int8 models with adapters via OpenVINO. It costs a small fine-tuning effort runnable on a laptop iGPU plus a 17-19% runtime generation-speed penalty when the adapter is applied. It can fail on errors the adapters do not fix — the paper shows signal and noise construction errors persist — and gains measured on 66 examples may not transfer to other domains, coding conventions, or model versions.
rationale: QLoRA SFT on small edge models demonstrably doubles pass rates on a narrow code domain using hardware the reader already has, and it fits constrained infrastructure, but the tiny 66-example dataset and modest absolute accuracy require validation on the reader's own task distribution before production use.
technique: QLoRA SFT of edge LLMs for domain code generation

claims.statement: The method replaces prompting an unadapted small edge model for domain-specific code generation with QLoRA/LoRA supervised fine-tuning on a small checked dataset, deployed as int8 models with adapters via OpenVINO. It costs a small fine-tuning effort runnable on a laptop iGPU plus a 17-19% runtime generation-speed penalty when the adapter is applied. It can fail on errors the adapters do not fix — the paper shows signal and noise construction errors persist — and gains measured on 66 examples may not transfer to other domains, coding conventions, or model versions.

Held-out pass rate on 66 checked MATLAB DSP tasks rises from 18/66 to 37/66 (LoRA and QLoRA) for E2B and from 32/66 to 47/66 (QLoRA) for E4B; adapters remove most convention errors but few signal/noise construction errors, and cost 17-19% of generation speed at run time.
